commands.review_summary:
The PR makes managed-plugin recovery choose the highest discovered semver across flat and generation directories, then repoints a stale managed persisted record to that newer path.

PR surface: Source +65, Tests +223. Total +288 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. the stale-flat-plus-new-generation state is concretely described and supported by redacted live terminal output, but this review did not execute it against the current main checkout. The source path and focused regression fixtures make the failure source-reproducible.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow mechanical repair can preserve explicit persisted plugin selections while retaining the intended stale-generation recovery.

target.title: fix(plugins): load newest managed generation when a prior install lingers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #107228. After upgrading a long-lived install, a plugin's newly-installed
version can silently fail to take effect: `openclaw plugins inspect <id>
--runtime` reports the old version and `install`/`update`/sync appear to no-op.

Root cause: a managed install/update writes the new version into a distinct
managed project directory (an `__openclaw-generation__` dir) **without removing**
the prior flat project dir. The persisted install-index record keeps pointing at
the older, still-present directory. At load time `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`
(`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) reconciles the persisted
record against a fresh disk scan, but its self-heal branches only cover (a) the
persisted path being **gone** (`isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`), and (b) a
newer version at the **same** path. The upgrade case — persisted path still
present, the same plugin id discovered at a **different**, newer generation dir —
falls through to `return params.persisted`, so the runtime imports the stale
directory.

## Fix

1. **Recover the newest install, not an arbitrary one.**
   `buildRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` previously let whichever project root
   sorted last win for a given plugin id. Generation-dir suffixes are content
   hashes, so on-disk order is unrelated to version. It now folds records through
   `pickNewerRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`, keeping the highest semver across the
   legacy flat dir and every generation dir (ties still prefer the later
   candidate, preserving generation-over-flat behavior).
2. **Repoint to the newer managed install.** When the recovered managed install
   is a strictly newer version at a different path, adopt it — reusing the same
   `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmMetadata(..., { preservePersistedSpec: true })` the
   path-gone branch uses. Gated on `isManagedNpmInstallPath`, so it only applies
   to persisted records inside the managed npm root; intentional custom/outside
   npm installs are left untouched.

Because this is a recovery-layer self-heal, it also repairs installs that have
**already** diverged from an earlier upgrade, not just future ones.

## Evidence

Focused tests in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-generation-precedence.test.ts`:

- **repoints to a newer managed generation when the persisted install still
  exists** — the upgrade case with the old dir present on disk (not covered by
  `isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`); asserts `installPath` / `version` /
  `spec` / `resolvedSpec`.
- **adopts the highest version when several generations are present** — pins
  version-based (not sort-order) selection.
- **keeps a current managed install when only an older generation lingers** —
  guard against an older generation superseding a current install.
- **does not repoint an intentional custom npm install outside the managed
  root** — guard for the managed-path gate.

Local run (this checkout's `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper is missing a dep, so
invoked vitest directly):

```
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
    src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-generation-precedence.test.ts \
    src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

Confirmed the primary "repoints…" and "custom npm install outside the managed
root" tests **fail on unpatched code** (revert the source change → those tests go
red) and **pass with the fix**. Existing recovery/index suites
(`installed-plugin-index.test.ts`, `installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts`, …)
remain green.

**Real-world verification (redacted; full before/after terminal output in a PR
comment):** on a live install upgraded 2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1 where two bundled
providers' flat (2026.6.11) and `__openclaw-generation__` (2026.7.1) dirs coexist,
the **unpatched** runtime (`openclaw plugins inspect … --runtime`) loads
**2026.6.11 from the flat dir**; running the **patched** recovery against
byte-for-byte copies of those real directories resolves **2026.7.1 from the
generation dir** for both providers, while a custom install outside the managed
npm root is left unchanged.

## Scope / caveats

- **Downgrades are intentionally not auto-adopted.** If a persisted record is
  newer than a lingering directory, the persisted record is kept rather than
  silently downgrading; an explicit downgrade should update the persisted record
  at the install layer.
- This resolves the **load-time symptom** at the recovery layer. If the
  install/update flow should also repoint the persisted record when it writes a
  new generation dir, that is a complementary fix in the install pipeline.

target.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`hashFileContentsSync` in `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts` reads the entire file synchronously into memory with no size limit to compute a SHA-256 hash for approval fingerprinting. A user who runs `node ./10GB-script.js` as a `system.run` operand would cause Node to block the event loop and OOM the process before approval is even evaluated.

This is a security OOM/availability vector on the **hot approval path**:
- Called every `system.run` to fingerprint the script operand for approval binding
- Called again on every revalidation before execution
- File path is derived from user-supplied CLI argv — an attacker who controls the workspace can trivially OOM or stall the runtime

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded synchronous `readFileSync` on user-controlled paths is a known OOM vector. The fix must bound memory usage without changing the existing approval contract for large script operands. Asynchronous streaming SHA-256 satisfies both goals: it caps per-chunk memory and yields the event loop, while still supporting arbitrarily large approved scripts.

## What Changed

**`src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts`:**
- Renamed `hashFileContentsSync` → `hashFileContents` and made it asynchronous.
- Uses `fs.promises.open(..., O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)`, `handle.createReadStream()`, and `crypto.createHash("sha256")` so the hash is computed chunk-by-chunk without loading the whole file.
- Renamed `resolveMutableFileOperandSnapshotSync` → `resolveMutableFileOperandSnapshot` and made it asynchronous.
- Made `revalidateApprovedMutableFileOperand` asynchronous.
- Made `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan` asynchronous.
- Kept the existing error handling: a non-regular file or symlink (via `O_NOFOLLOW`) still returns a clean `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED` message.

**Callers updated to await the async boundary:**
- `src/node-host/invoke.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude-handler.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts`

**Tests updated:**
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts`

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `node ./10GB-script.js` -> OOM, process killed | `node ./10GB-script.js` -> hashed asynchronously, approval binding preserved |
| `node ./4MB-script.js` -> works (unchanged) | `node ./4MB-script.js` -> works (unchanged) |
| Error from non-regular operand -> unhandled exception | Error -> proper `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED` message |

The change is additive from a behavior perspective for legitimate large scripts; only the internal hashing boundary becomes async.

## Evidence (head SHA: `345759cee3b`)

### Focused Tests — all pass ✓

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts

 ✓ |unit-fast-isolated| src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts (20 tests)
 ✓ |unit-fast-isolated| src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts (72 tests)

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  92 passed (92)
```

### Terminal Proof — large operand approval + revalidation at current head

The transcript below executes the actual checked-in production modules at `345759cee3b` against a real 32 MiB script file.

```
$ node --import tsx/esm prove-110712-async-hash.mjs

=== 1. Large operand approval plan ===
plan.ok: true
mutableFileOperand.path: /tmp/oc-approval-hash-g4tlhp/big-script.js
mutableFileOperand.argvIndex: 1
mutableFileOperand.sha256 (prefix): 5e478e0aff2a4e45...

=== 2. Verify hash matches crypto.hash ===
expected: 5e478e0aff2a4e45...
actual:   5e478e0aff2a4e45...
match: true

=== 3. Revalidation succeeds before execution ===
revalidate: true

=== 4. Snapshot helper directly ===
snapshot.ok: true
snapshot.sha256 (prefix): 5e478e0aff2a4e45...
```

The proof runner imports `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan`, `revalidateApprovedMutableFileOperand`, and `resolveMutableFileOperandSnapshot` directly from `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts` and invokes them against real files. No inlined copies or mocks.
